function.name: research_lookup
function.description: Research already held for this question: call FIRST with the question restated to stand alone. Returns [P#] passages earlier answers to it used (curated sets first), or that none is held.

question.description: The reader's question, restated to stand alone

function.name: book_card
function.description: THE BOOK ITSELF: use only when the reader wants the book (to read it, to have it). Resolves a title (any spelling) among the library's works and sections and shows the reader its card. Returns a [B#].

title.description: The work's title as the library catalogues it

function.name: search_in_work
function.description: Search INSIDE one work (Star of the West = all its issues; years narrow them). Give several differently worded queries in the words the SOURCE would use (a 1910 birth notice says "a daughter was born", not "birth"); each is searched as exact words AND by meaning, in parallel, merged and deduped. Returns [P#] with their place.

years.description: A periodical: only these years (Star of the West: 1910 = volume 1)

section.description: One part of the work, by its title

function.name: find_passage
function.description: Find the passage that holds given words (exact first, then closest in meaning), across the library or held to a tradition, an author or one work. Use when the reader quotes or describes a passage. Returns [P#].

query.description: The words to find, as the text would say them

function.name: extract_from_work
function.description: A SELECTION from one whole work: read it through and pick what was asked ("the prayers in it", "every mention of the Greatest Name"). Returns the picked [P#] in reading order. Slow: for a selection, not a search.

select.description: What to pick out of it

function.name: fused_search
function.description: Search the library (primary texts in English, and in their original Arabic/Persian for the Bahá’í Writings only, authorised interpretation, history, scholarship), every layer fused on the query as written: no planner, no LLM. Phrase the query in the words the texts themselves would use; narrow with filters (author, work, authority, tradition, years, language) and pick layers to run only some.

query.description: Words to search for, as the texts would say them

filters.description: Hard filters, the same for every passage search.

author.description: Author (writer or quoted voice), e.g. Bahá'u'lláh; a list = any of them

writerOnly.description: The author must be the writer, not a quoted voice

language.description: ISO code, e.g. en, ar, fa

documentId.description: Only this document; a list = any of them

work.description: Only this work, by title in any spelling (resolved to its document)

authority.description: Only passages of these standings (Passage.authority), e.g. ["scripture","interpretation"]

yearTo.description: Documents dated up to this year

layers.description: Run only these layers and merge them (literal = exact words, no embedding; phrase = meaning of a phrase; hype = questions answered; originals = the Bahá’í Persian/Arabic Writings ONLY — skipped when the tradition is another). Omit = every layer fused.

tiers.description: Escalation ladder: if fewer than min_results come back, drop these filters one at a time in this order and search again; each passage says its tier (strict | relaxed:<dropped filters>). Omit = filters are hard.

spell.description: Correct misspellings against the library vocabulary before searching (deterministic; query_used says what was searched)

function.name: originals_search
function.description: Bahá'í Persian/Arabic originals ONLY (no other tradition has an originals index here; another tradition's filter returns an empty list with `unavailable`). Search the Writings of the Báb, Bahá'u'lláh, 'Abdu'l-Bahá and Shoghi Effendi in their ORIGINAL Persian and Arabic. Words in English (the phrase layer matches across languages) or in Persian/Arabic. A hit with no linked translation is the original alone.

query.description: Words to search for, as the texts would say them

function.name: context_lookup
function.description: Read the paragraphs before and after a passage you found (its ref, e.g. P3) — for context, or to see how a thought continues.

function.name: whole_lookup
function.description: Read the whole prayer that a found passage (its ref) belongs to — every paragraph, nothing shortened.

function.name: original_lookup
function.description: The original-language (Arabic/Persian) text of an English passage, and the authorised translations linked to that original. Give the English words (a sentence or two).

english.description: The English words (a sentence or two)

tradition.description: Another tradition than the Bahá’í: its own work family is used (editions aligned by verse/section, else meaning)

function.name: translation_lookup
function.description: An EXISTING English translation of an Arabic/Persian text (a prayer, tablet or passage the reader gives in the original): the library's original paragraph and the translations linked to it — authorized (Shoghi Effendi, the Bahá'í World Centre), published, or Stephen Phelps' provisional renderings. Give the original text (a line or more, in Arabic script). Call it BEFORE translating anything yourself.

original.description: The original text (a line or more, Arabic script)

tradition.description: Another tradition than the Bahá’í: its own work family is used (editions aligned by verse/section, else meaning)

function.name: rendering_lookup
function.description: How Shoghi Effendi rendered an Arabic/Persian word or root across the Writings (the CTAI concordance): his English renderings with counts, and passages pairing the original with his English. Give the word in ARABIC SCRIPT.

term_arabic.description: The word or root in Arabic script

translator.description: Keep only passages rendered by this translator, e.g. Shoghi Effendi

function.name: source_trace
function.description: A House of Justice letter, a scholar or a compilation stating a teaching is a SIGNPOST (Chad 10-19: when they refer to the teachings there is a presumption they mean something specific — we hold it): give its ref (e.g. P4) and get the primary passages it quotes or rests on — from the library's quote links, else the closest scripture and authorised interpretation of the signpost's tradition (default Bahá'í: Bahá'u'lláh, the Báb, 'Abdu'l-Bahá, Shoghi Effendi; pass `tradition` for another). Cite THOSE.

function.name: quotation_candidates
function.description: Candidates for where a quotation comes from: its published source (core literature), the original-language tablet, other works quoting it; each with a score (the share of the quotation’s words the passage holds). Judging which candidate is right is the caller’s decision.

quotation.description: The quotation as the reader gave it

tradition.description: The tradition the reader named (any): its own core is the source, its own-language edition the original. Absent = the whole library

function.name: document_search
function.description: A WORK in the library by its title (any spelling: "Dawnbreakers", "Book of Certitude", "Iqan"): the library's copy with its link. When nothing matches well, the few closest titles come back marked match "close": a name is evidence, not identity — they are spelling candidates for you to judge by author, language and what was asked, never a confirmed hit. When the reader asks for a book — to read it, find it, get a copy, a link — give THIS link; never send them to another site or catalog.

function.name: work_notes_lookup
function.description: What the sources say about a CORE work's significance, purpose, station or impression (the Aqdas, the Íqán, the Hidden Words, God Passes By, The Dawn-Breakers…): verified quotations, best authority first. Call it beside document_search when a reader asks for or about a book.

title.description: The work, any spelling or alias

function.name: web_search
function.description: The open web — ONLY for what a library of texts cannot hold (recent events, modern scholarship, general background). Results are labelled WEB and never treated as scripture or authoritative.
